topics.topic: Determination and DNS safety of the plain-HTTP loopback exception
questions: Does this mean only a literal loopback IP in the URL, a hostname that resolves exclusively to loopback, or the actual connected address, and is it rechecked after DNS resolution?
How is the loopback exception decided and protected against DNS changes between checking and connecting?
How is the loopback exception determined and protected against DNS changes?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about which hosts qualify for the plain-HTTP loopback exception.

precedent.topic: Definition and DNS handling of the plain-HTTP loopback exception
quotes:
Plain `http` is allowed only for an instance of
   class `local_dev` or `disposable_rig`, as the manifest instance's `class`
   states — an absent or unknown class counts as `production` — or one whose
   `api_base_url` host is a loopback address; any other plain `http` target is refused before sending.
precedent.why: The definition of loopback concerns unchanged text and was not made material by the change.

topics.topic: Filesystem access allowed to sandboxed agent code
questions: May agent code itself read or write paths in the exchange directory, or may only the sandbox runner use that directory?
What filesystem access is agent-written code actually allowed?
May agent code read or write the exchange directory and read arbitrary runtime files, or must those paths be accessible only to the runner?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about filesystem access available to sandboxed function code.

precedent.topic: Sandboxed function access to runtime files and the exchange directory
quotes:
A function node runs one admitted implementation of one contract: declared input
in, declared output out, no network, no filesystem beyond its input, no clock, no
randomness, no secret, no service handle.
precedent.why: The filesystem restriction was unchanged, and the change did not alter sandbox path access.

topics.topic: Multipart field-name and media-type encoding and framing
questions: How are quotes, backslashes, non-ASCII characters and line breaks in port names handled when constructing multipart headers?
Which port names and media-type strings are safe to place in multipart headers, and are unsafe values escaped or refused when the contract or binding is authored?
What port-name and media-type grammar, quoting, boundary generation and CRLF framing produce the multipart bytes?

judgement.why: Multipart header escaping, media-type grammar, boundary generation and wire framing are format and encoding decisions belonging to State 6 or later.

topics.topic: Ownership and permission requirements for the data directory and files
questions: What exact ownership and permission checks define “private,” including permissions on directories, the SQLite database, spool files and content files?
What exact filesystem metadata must the data directory, its subdirectories and files satisfy at start?
What filesystem ownership and permission conditions must hold for the data directory and each contained file?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about the ownership and permission rules meant by private kernel storage.

precedent.topic: Ownership, file-type, and permission requirements for private data storage
quotes:
The directory and everything in it
   are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.
precedent.why: The exact meaning of private filesystem state was already unspecified in this unchanged passage.

topics.topic: Reading manifest files at a configured revision
questions: How is a manifest file read at a revision, and what happens when the location is not a supported repository, the revision is unknown, or the file at that revision cannot be obtained?
What exact mechanism reads a manifest file at a configured revision and what conditions make that read fail?
How exactly does the kernel read a file at `manifest_revision`?

judgement.why: This is the same question about resolving and reading the configured manifest revision, already decided by later text.

precedent.topic: Loading, validation, and change semantics of the configured manifest revision
quotes:
**The manifest at a revision**: `manifest_location` is a directory inside a
   git repository and `manifest_revision` a commit of it; `bindings` reads
   `<service_id>.json` of that directory at that commit as a git object, never
   from the working tree, so a record changes only with the configured revision
   (A08 rules 1 and 6).

**A manifest that cannot be read at start** in
   `bindings.check_installed_instances`: the start stops and names it; every
   start step is required (State 3, "Start").
precedent.why: The later text defines revision reads as Git-object reads at a commit and makes an unreadable startup manifest stop startup.

topics.topic: Required and permitted port coverage in authored trial cases
questions: Must authored inputs contain exactly every input port and no unknown ports, and, when expected_outputs is present, must it contain exactly every output port or may it assert only a subset?
Must trial inputs name exactly every input port, and when `expected_outputs` is present must it name exactly every output port?
What port presence and extra-key rules apply to authored trial cases?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about the exact required and permitted fields of authored trial cases.

precedent.topic: Required and allowed TrialCase input and expected-output port sets
precedent.why: Required and optional request fields and the exact trial-case input and expected-output shapes belong to State 6 schemas.

topics.topic: Valid HTTP header values and their byte encoding
questions: Which character encoding and HTTP-field-value grammar apply to non-ASCII required-header values, and when is an unencodable value refused?
What characters are legal in required and credential header values, and what exact bytes are sent for non-ASCII text?
Which header-value characters and encodings are accepted, and what happens when the HTTP client cannot transmit a value verbatim?

judgement.why: The character grammar and byte encoding of HTTP header values are format and encoding decisions belonging to State 6 or later.

topics.topic: Valid api_base_url forms, normalization, and path joining
questions: Are user information, an existing path, query, fragment, repeated trailing slashes, noncanonical ports and internationalized host names allowed in api_base_url, and exactly how are they joined and represented in Host and approval data?
Which exact `api_base_url` forms are valid and how is the request URL joined without library-specific normalization?
What exact grammar and normalization rules apply to `api_base_url` before joining the declared path?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about canonical base-URL syntax, normalization and operation-path joining.

precedent.topic: Canonical api_base_url syntax and operation-path joining
precedent.why: The accepted base-URL grammar, joining rules and Host serialization are format and encoding details belonging to State 6.

topics.topic: Complete prohibition of clock and elapsed-time observation
questions: Are unlisted clock and elapsed-resource-time APIs allowed because the trap list is closed, or must every way of observing time be blocked?
Is the closed trap list the complete meaning of “no clock”, or must every route by which code can observe time be unavailable?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about enforcing the no-clock and deterministic-execution requirements against unlisted observations.

precedent.topic: Enforcement of determinism against all clocks, randomness, and other observable nondeterminism
quotes: The same implementation on the same input yields the same output digest twice.
precedent.why: The determinism requirement and its enforcement question predated the change and were untouched by it.

topics.topic: Determinism requirement and sandbox enforcement property
questions: Is deterministic output an enforced requirement for every admitted implementation, and if so, what additional capabilities or observations are prohibited or checked?
What property must the sandbox enforce to make cross-execution output determinism a real invariant?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about guaranteeing deterministic execution of allowed Python code.

precedent.topic: Guaranteeing deterministic execution of allowed Python code
quotes: The same implementation on the same input yields the same output digest twice.
precedent.why: The determinism requirement and its enforcement question predated the change and were untouched by it.

topics.topic: Durable representation of empty mapped file outputs
questions: How does a NodeExecution durably represent an empty `many` file output and its disclosure class?
How is an empty `many` file output represented durably in a NodeExecution?

quotes:
`SpooledFilesRef`
    gains `disclosure_class`, the class of the file list it names, so an empty
    list keeps the class A13 rule 6 gives it and counts in an execution's
    class (A07 rule 5).
judgement.why: The later contract gives an empty file list a durable SpooledFilesRef carrying its disclosure class.

topics.topic: Durable storage of mapped file-list disclosure class
questions: Where is the class of a non-empty mapped file list recorded so it can be recovered and verified after restart?
Where is the disclosure class of a mapped file list stored so it can be reconstructed after restart?

quotes:
`SpooledFilesRef`
    gains `disclosure_class`, the class of the file list it names, so an empty
    list keeps the class A13 rule 6 gives it and counts in an execution's
    class (A07 rule 5).
judgement.why: The later contract records the aggregate file-list class on SpooledFilesRef.

topics.topic: Encoding of path placeholders and validation of static path escapes
questions: What exact byte-to-URL encoding is used for path placeholders, and which characters or percent escapes are valid in the static declared path?
What exact text is percent-encoded for an integer path placeholder?

quotes: prepare_request: [BEHAVIOR] Builds the URL as base_url without one trailing slash followed by the declared path, each placeholder segment replaced by its input value, which must be a non-null string or an integer written in decimal, UTF-8 percent-encoded except the RFC 3986 unreserved characters so that it stays one segment; nothing else in the URL is normalized.

read_manifest_operation: [VALIDATION_ERROR] After read_service_record, raises RefusedError naming the first failing check in this order: no capability has the operation name; its effect_class is not a member of = models.EffectClass; it is not invocable because http_api is not exactly one route made of a method in = models.HttpMethod, one ASCII space and a path; the path does not start with one slash, contains a double slash, a dot or dot-dot segment, a question mark, a hash, a scheme or a host, or has a brace outside a placeholder, an empty or malformed placeholder, or one placeholder name twice; for an effect_class other than read, the idempotency_key text split on plus with each part trimmed has an empty part, a repeated name, or a name that is not a plain identifier of a letter or underscore followed by letters, digits or underscores.
judgement.why: The later notes define placeholder spelling and encoding and the validation applied to the static declared path.

topics.topic: Equality semantics for guard values
questions: What equality relation is used for JSON guard values, especially numbers such as 1 and 1.0 and composite enum values?
What equality relation decides a guard, including cases such as `1` versus `1.0` and objects with different member order?

quotes:
JSON a record holds as a fact — a `value_schema`, a
guard value — is canonical JSON text, so "the same schema" is equal text
(A05 rule 2). `module:surface` turns every JSON text of a request into
canonical form before any module sees it (State 5, "Values enter canonical").

advance_run: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] The next node is the ready node with the smallest node_id; a node is ready when every input port holds its value: flow inputs delivered along every edge from them, constants to their port, and outputs of a concluded succeeded node along every edge whose guard is absent or whose guard port value equals the guard value as canonical JSON text.
judgement.why: The later contract compares produced and declared guard values as canonical JSON text.

topics.topic: Implementations eligible for rollback
questions: What makes an implementation “earlier”: submission before the current implementation, any previously submitted non-current implementation, or any implementation previously activated for that contract version?
Which implementations are eligible for rollback besides having an admitted verdict over the current corpus?

quotes: roll_back_slot: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Raises UnknownReferenceError for an unknown slot, then for an unknown implementation; then RefusedError when the implementation belongs to a contract version other than the slot's current one, and RefusedError when it holds no admitted verdict over the current corpus digest; it runs no admission.

roll_back_slot: [BEHAVIOR] Naming the implementation that is already the current activation returns that Activation and records nothing; otherwise one RecordActivationChange is written through record_change with activated_at from kernel_now and the given actor.
judgement.why: The later API makes every implementation of the current contract version with an admitted verdict over the current corpus eligible, with the already-current implementation treated as a no-op.

topics.topic: Resource ceilings for manifests and request construction
questions: What bounds apply to manifest data before parsing, hashing, storing it in previews or using it to build HTTP requests?
What release ceilings bound manifest files, capability entries, instance headers and approval-preview request descriptions, and what refusal occurs when one is exceeded?

judgement.divergence: One implementer accepts and processes arbitrarily large manifest records and header values, potentially creating arbitrarily large approval records or exhausting kernel resources; another imposes local limits and refuses the same manifest or binding, which the owner and proposing agent notice and which can affect kernel availability.
judgement.why: No release ceiling or refusal rule bounds manifest files, capability entries, instance headers or the request descriptions derived from them.

topics.topic: Supported JSON Schema subset for operation-binding ports
questions: Must every binding port's value_schema be validated against the same supported JSON Schema subset as a contract port?
Must a binding proposal be refused when an input or output schema is outside the kernel's supported subset?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about applying the supported JSON Schema subset to operation-binding ports.

precedent.topic: Contract-port validation rules and ordering for operation bindings
quotes:
Any other keyword —
   `$ref`, `pattern`, `format`, `oneOf`, `anyOf`, `allOf`, `not` among them —
   is outside the subset: A02 refuses it in a contract version, and
   `fit_port_value` answers that no value fits it, so a binding or flow port
   written outside the subset can never deliver.
precedent.why: State 6 specifies that contracts refuse unsupported schemas while binding and flow ports may contain them but can never deliver a fitting value.

topics.topic: Use of file outputs as guards
questions: May a file output be used as a guard, and if so, what value is compared with the declared guard member?
Can a `file` output port be used as a guard, and if not, in which proof phase is it refused?

quotes:
A closed set (A05 guards) is a schema with `enum`
   or `const`. A `file` port's `value_schema` is the empty schema `{}`; its fit
   is its media type (State 5, `fit_port_value`).
judgement.why: The later contract fixes every file port's schema as the empty schema, which is not a closed set and therefore cannot satisfy the guard check.

topics.topic: Accounting semantics for memory_bytes and process_count
questions: What exactly is counted by `memory_bytes` and `process_count`, especially for a contract with `process_count = 1`?

topics.topic: Atomicity and checking order for mapped-output aggregation failures
questions: If one mapped output list is within the bound and another is over it, are any valid outputs delivered or exposed before the node is derived as failed, and in what port order are lists checked?

topics.topic: Audit events and path-resolution cases recorded as sandbox violations
questions: Exactly which Python audit events and filesystem path-resolution cases must record a sandbox violation?

topics.topic: Behavior when rebuilding a not_applied resend fails pre-send checks
questions: After resolving `not_applied`, what happens if rebuilding the resend fails a pre-send check?

topics.topic: Canonical ordering of unordered lists for identity hashing
questions: What exact comparison orders every unordered list before identity hashing?

topics.topic: Classification of resource exhaustion and ambiguous process exits
questions: What observations classify an execution as `resource_exhausted`, and how are ambiguous process exits classified?

topics.topic: Crash atomicity of admission verdict persistence and activation
questions: Can an admitted verdict persist without its required activation after a crash?

topics.topic: Disclosed length for non-open failure details
questions: What exact length is disclosed for a non-open failure detail?

topics.topic: Distinguishing an empty node_id from a flow endpoint
questions: May a flow node use the empty string as its `node_id`, and if so how is it distinguished from a flow endpoint?

topics.topic: Enforcement of repair versus composition inspection authority
questions: How does the kernel enforce the difference between repair inspection and composition inspection for the same agent token?

topics.topic: Handling HTTP-client normalization that changes on-wire requests
questions: What happens if the HTTP stack rewrites the URL, Host value, header whitespace, percent escapes or transfer framing so that the on-wire request differs from the described request?

topics.topic: Handling and bounding stdout and stderr
questions: What happens to stdout and stderr while code runs, and what prevents unbounded output from blocking the child or consuming host memory or disk?

topics.topic: Linking a draft-write send to its authorizing FlowActivation
questions: How does a later draft-write send identify the exact FlowActivation that authorized its run?

topics.topic: Ordering and reporting of multiple kernel startup failures
questions: When several startup conditions fail, which check runs first and which failure is reported?

topics.topic: Ordering event for concurrent requests
questions: What observable event fixes the order of concurrent requests?

topics.topic: Outcome and check ordering for non-canonical Python return values
questions: Which execution outcome applies when a returned value cannot be represented as canonical JSON, and does this check occur before output-size accounting?

topics.topic: Precedence and observability of spool-file and response-size ceilings
questions: Is `spool_file_bytes_max` intended to be independently observable, and which limit wins when the service-response and spool-file ceilings are crossed together?

topics.topic: Presence and type rules for idempotency_key
questions: How are an absent idempotency_key and values of other JSON types handled for read and non-read operations?

topics.topic: Proof-failure precedence when an edge has multiple endpoint defects
questions: Which reason is returned when more than one endpoint defect exists on the first edge?

topics.topic: ProofResult subject identity for non-node failures
questions: What exact subject does a ProofResult name for failures that belong to a constant, port, flow endpoint, or repeated name?

topics.topic: Query encoding semantics for cardinality and array-valued schemas
questions: How do port cardinality and an array-valued schema combine when encoding query parameters?

topics.topic: Ready-set eligibility and re-eligibility of nodes
questions: Are concluded and waiting non-mapped nodes excluded from the ready set, and exactly when do approval, resolution or resume make one eligible again?

topics.topic: Retention, accounting, and cleanup of unrecorded attempt files
questions: Are partial or otherwise unrecorded files from service_unreachable, outcome_unknown, crashes and interrupted attempts retained and counted, and how are they identified for replacement and startup cleanup without a record?

topics.topic: Retry behavior after a resumed send remains unreachable
questions: If a resumed send again ends service_unreachable, is it attempted once and left waiting, or immediately selected again within the same resume request?

topics.topic: Reuse of removed agent identities
questions: May an agent name be reused after its token is removed, even though historical records would then not distinguish the old and new agents?

topics.topic: Rollback validation order and first refusal
questions: What is the exact check order and first refusal for rollback?

topics.topic: Scope of response secrecy and payload scanning
questions: Does this rule prohibit only kernel-generated disclosure of protected configuration and internal diagnostics, or must arbitrary returned payloads be scanned and withheld?

topics.topic: Startup behavior when a selected service instance is absent
questions: Does a configured service or instance name that is absent from the manifest stop kernel startup, count as no selected instance, or fail only operations for that service?

topics.topic: Store-position assignment for atomic creations and mutations
questions: How are unique store positions assigned and ordered when one atomic store call creates several records, and do mutations receive new positions?

topics.topic: Supported JSON Schema subset for flow ports
questions: Must composition reject a flow port whose schema is outside the supported JSON Schema subset?

topics.topic: TLS verification policy
questions: Which trust anchors, hostname rules, certificate-time source, protocol versions and client-certificate behavior define a verified TLS connection?

topics.topic: Timestamp recorded when an unknown effect attempt is resolved
questions: When the owner resolves an unknown attempt, does concluded_at remain the time it first became unknown, change to the resolution time, or is the resolution time intentionally unrecorded?

topics.topic: Validation of resubmitted contracts against lowered ceilings
questions: After a release lowers a ceiling, does resubmitting content equal to an existing older contract return that contract or fail current-ceiling validation?

topics.topic: Visibility of branch selection by personal-data guards
questions: May an agent observe which branch a personal-data guard selected?

topics.topic: Whether all randomness APIs or only nondeterministic randomness are forbidden
questions: Does “no randomness” forbid all random APIs, or only entropy and unseeded nondeterminism?

topics.topic: Whether path-placeholder inputs may have cardinality many
questions: May a path-placeholder input have cardinality `many`?
